conclusion.decision: G0 remains open; this audit does not freeze 30 fps or make it the default mode.
conclusion.summary: With the AX7020 dual-sample timing values and an assumed 84 MHz PCLK, doubling VTS from 740 to 1480 gives 29.9982858122 fps by the timing formula. This arithmetic does not validate a 720p30 OV5640 operating mode.

page_evidence.visual_and_text_check: 720p is 1280x720 at 60 fps with 96/192 MHz pixel clock; 1080p is 1920x1080 at 30 fps with 96/192 MHz pixel clock.
page_evidence.bearing: The datasheet's standard-mode table does not establish 720p30.

page_evidence.reference: Table 4-2, image windowing registers, sheet 2 of 2
page_evidence.visual_and_text_check: Registers 0x380E and 0x380F are RW TIMING VTS high and low bytes, together representing total vertical size[15:0].
page_evidence.bearing: RW access establishes programmability, not validation of a particular altered timing configuration.

page_evidence.visual_and_text_check: If manual exposure must exceed the predefined frame period, the maximum frame value in 0x380E/0x380F must be set first, then exposure may be set in 0x3500-0x3502.
page_evidence.bearing: This describes register ordering for extended manual exposure; it does not prove 30 fps output, AEC behavior, or the proposed dual-sensor setup.

clock_basis_difference.datasheet_basis: PDF p.22 Table 2-1 lists 720p at 96/192 MHz pixel clock and 60 fps.
clock_basis_difference.sample_basis: The dual-sample source comment at line 258 says PCLK=84 MHz for its PLL configuration.
clock_basis_difference.audit_rule: 84 MHz is treated only as an unverified arithmetic assumption from a source comment; it is not treated as a measured or reconciled DVP PCLK. The datasheet and sample clock figures must be reconciled for the exact PLL/divider/output-clock semantics before adopting a frame-rate claim.

assumptions: PCLK is exactly 84000000 Hz, based only on the dual-sample source comment.
Changing VTS alone does not change the active PCLK, HTS, output format, or other timing behavior.

30fps_arithmetic_candidate.meaning: Arithmetic candidate only under the 84 MHz assumption; not a validated sensor mode or selected project default.

aec_banding_arithmetic_under_same_assump.interpretation: These are arithmetic summaries of the current source values, not proof of OV5640 AEC/banding behavior after VTS is changed to 1480.

unverified_items: Whether the 84 MHz source comment matches the actual sensor PCLK and how it relates to the datasheet's 96/192 MHz 720p pixel-clock entries.
Whether the proposed VTS=0x05C8 with the exact PLL, HTS, crop/binning, and output configuration produces the expected 720p30 DVP timing.
AEC/AGC and manual-exposure limits after VTS changes, including 0x3A02/03, 0x3A14/15, band-step and maximum-band settings, night-mode behavior, and 50/60 Hz flicker response.
DVP PCLK, HREF, VSYNC, active-pixel/line timing, and any sensor-specific constraints under the candidate settings.
Initialization and sustained frame-rate stability of both sensors together, including synchronization, frame alignment, capture buffering, and drop behavior.

work_performed.scope: Read-only feasibility audit of the existing README draft against the fixed OV5640 datasheet and AX7020 official dual-sample source.
operations: Verified repository HEAD/branch, official source-cache commit and clean status, PDF SHA-256, parser-manifest SHA-256/status, and dual-sample source SHA-256.
Read the README candidate line and relevant dual-sample register sequence; visually checked rendered OV5640 PDF pages 22, 42, and 50 against extracted text.
Calculated current and candidate frame-rate arithmetic and summarized the existing AEC/banding register values under the stated 84 MHz assumption.

test_boundaries: No Vivado/Vitis build, synthesis, timing analysis, programming, board/JTAG operation, or Batch109 access was performed.
No register sequence was implemented or changed, and no camera mode was frozen or selected.
No test in this audit validates electrical limits, actual sensor clocks, DVP timing, image quality, AEC/banding response, or dual-camera stability.
